title: What If Betelgeuse Replaced the Sun? Earth Would Be Inside It

scenes.text: What if Betelgeuse replaced the Sun? Earth would be inside the star.
Betelgeuse is a red supergiant roughly 900 to 1,000 times wider than the Sun, about 600 light-years away.
Put it where the Sun is, and its surface reaches somewhere between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars would all be swallowed.
Its surface is cooler, about 3,200 degrees Celsius, but it shines about 135,000 times brighter than the Sun.
Most calculations say it will explode as a supernova within a million years. You wouldn't see it coming. You'd be inside it.
